chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'Every road that is trodden upon and used as a pathway, whether it has a main avenue in it or not, it is not befitting for the prayer to be performed in it.' I said, 'So where should I pray?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'On the right and on the left.'

key_terms.يَمْنَةً وَ يَسْرَةً: on the right and on the left

ai.seo_question: Where is it appropriate to perform prayer if not on a frequently used road?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that any path frequently trodden by people, whether a main thoroughfare or a minor track, is unsuitable for prayer to preserve its sanctity from distraction and disrespect. His directive to pray 'on the right and left' (yamanatan wa yasaran) provides a practical spatial solution, indicating that one should step aside to the edges of the path rather than remaining in the center of the flow of traffic. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *khushu'* (focus) and the physical dignity of the prayer space, distinguishing between the public domain of movement and the private domain of worship.
